GLASSMAN / CF Journal opening (domain: GPP, metcon, gymnastics):
1) Week: 'five or six days' is sanctioned, 5-on/2-off explicitly allowed (Template 2003, prof s5). Mon-Sat fits. Sessions capped at 60 min: 'past one hour, more is not better' (Foundations).
2) Session shape: warmup, lift (Wendler slot), then 'a tight little couplet or triplet' (Virtuosity 2005; s5). That leaves ~20-25 min. Mon-Fri: 3-4 metcons/wk after the lift. Alternate (a) task-priority couplet, 3-5 rounds for time, 'first round hard but possible', 2-10 min, glycolytic; (b) time-priority triplet, 20 min AMRAP, light-moderate. Use M/G/W rotation from the Template.
3) Loads: no percentages in source (s8). Scale load first so round 1 finishes 'without compromising form or reaching muscular failure' (Scaling). [INFERENCE] formula: metcon set = floor(0.5 x max strict pull-ups); barbell load chosen to pass that rule, logged.
4) Gymnastics every metcon: one mastered plus one developing element (s5). Ladders as tests: pull-ups 20/25/30, L-hold in 30 s steps.
5) Benchmarks: Fran, Grace, Diane reappear irregularly; no special prep; progress = T1/T2 power ratio (Benchmark Workouts 2003; s6).
6) Conditioning: 'bulk of metabolic training should be interval training'; 5-6 short efforts per long one (Foundations).
7) Isolation bodybuilding 'has no place' (s7). Replace with compound gymnastics.
Athlete's anti-random principle: source says 'routine is the enemy', but the Template is 'randomized within some parameters'. I accept a fixed structure with varied exercise selection.

Expected conflicts: Seiler (oxidative volume vs 'excessive oxidative training' fault); Wendler (fixed scheme vs variance; I accept the lift slot as the heavy-W element); any coach who keeps isolation hypertrophy work.

PROFILE DONE: /Users/jason/Documents/golden-hour/profiles/nick-bare.md

BARE OPENING (hypertrophy plus lift/run scheduling):
1) Frequency: 3 strength days at Bare's stated minimum. He cut from 5 to 3 when adding running and says you can't tack a 5-day lift week onto a 5-day run week (InsideHook 2023). Add 3+ aerobic sessions, which can be any modality (Build video).
2) Order: quad-dominant day early in the week, hinge day nearest the long run (BPN 2026: quads hurt running more). Mon squat, Wed press, Fri deadlift, Sat long run. Never put the hard run on a squat or deadlift day (BPN: separate hard runs and heavy lifts).
3) Assistance fixes the lag in the lifts. After the Wendler lift, use the ~15 min left for 2 compound-led accessories at 3-4 x 8-12, on the muscles of the day's CFT lift (quads, posterior chain, delts/triceps), plus pull-up volume. Progression: when the top of the rep range moves cleanly, add load; with home DBs capped at 80 lb, add reps/sets instead (Lift Vault 16-wk). Target about 10 hard sets/muscle/week, the low end of his 10-20 (ep. 185, snippet-verified only). Last set near failure [INFERENCE: no explicit RIR in source].
4) Runs: easy runs stay truly easy, Zone 2 / below MAF ('biggest mistake: easy runs too hard'). At most 1 quality run plus the Saturday long run. Mileage up no more than 10%/wk.
5) Autoregulate: after poor sleep or soreness, cut intensity or swap the run for the bike.
6) Track body weight/body composition monthly (6 Pillars).

EXPECTED CONFLICTS: wendler (BBB/FSL vs bodybuilding-style assistance; % vs rep-range progression), glassman (fatigue-driven varied metcons; BPN: 'fatigue alone is not progress'), first (3 hard runs/wk vs Bare's mostly-easy running).

WENDLER EVO 5 (strength):
1) Lifts: squat, press, DL, 1 main lift/day, 3 days. Suggested Mon squat, Wed press, Thu DL. Jumps first: 10-15 box jumps (Beginners post).
2) TM = 0.85 x tested 1RM, down from 0.90 ('start too light', 'A higher TM does not equal more strength'). With 3 runs a week he would go lower, not higher (Running Hills essay).
3) 16 wks, Forever structure [SECONDARY]: Leader wk1-3, Leader wk4-6, wk7 deload (40/50/60x5), Anchor wk8-10, wk11 TM test (70/80/90x5, then 100% TM: fewer than 3 reps means TM comes down), Anchor wk12-14, wk15 deload, wk16 retest.
   Leader = 5's PRO + 5x5 FSL (65/70/75%), no AMRAP.
   Anchor = 5/3/1 with PR set on wk1 & wk3, Jokers +5-10% only on strong days, 3x5 FSL.
   Fits the 12-15 min slot. BBB rejected: it needs more recovery next to running.
4) The 'missing volume' answer is supplemental FSL, not bodybuilding. Assistance per lift day: push/pull/single-leg-core, 25-50 reps each in Leader, 50-100 in Anchor. Pull-ups = the pull assistance.
5) Progression: +5 lb press, +10 lb squat/DL each 3-wk cycle, only if all reps are clean. No grinding or missed reps. A failed TM test means TM -10%.
6) Conditioning: hard work on squat/DL days. Wendler: 'Never do conditioning the day before lower body lifting.' Strictly that means no Sun/Wed conditioning; with 6 days I'd accept easy only on Tue/Wed [INFERENCE].
CONFLICTS: glassman (metcon intensity/placement before leg days), seiler/first (where hard runs sit vs squat/DL), hinshaw (lift volume/frequency for hybrid).

HINSHAW, Evo 5 aerobic recommendations:
1) TEST: Hinshaw diagnoses with a max 400 plus a max mile. FF = ln(Tmile/T400)/ln(4.02) - 1, target 20-22% (Profile s4.2-3, s6). The mile is not in the battery, so run a mile time trial in week 1 and retest it in weeks 4, 8, 12 (PROJECT PB tests the mile at about week 4). Until it is logged, predicted mile = T400 x 4.02^1.215, about 5.4 x T400 [INFERENCE]. Using the 10k as a proxy gives FF of about 18% [INFERENCE], so the 400-to-mile range is the gap to check.
2) RUN FREQUENCY: his running program is 2 quality sessions/week, low volume, 'you can't train a CrossFit athlete like a triathlete' (s5). On the new frequency note: his program does not support 3+ runs as necessary.
Tue: speed gears, e.g. Bombolini (3x[500 m between mile and 400 pace, 200 m jog, 100 m at or under 400 pace], 5 min between sets) or a Froning-style 600/400/300/200 ladder, rest equal to work.
Thu: threshold gears, e.g. Hop Scotch (5.9 km).
Sat (optional third run): easy long run at recovery-jog pace.
About 25-30 min of work per session.
3) PACING: never run faster than the prescription; 1 s too fast costs recovery (s5). Paces reset after each mile retest. Reference rate: Froning gained about 5% in 12 weeks.
4) Stacking intervals with lifts is acceptable (Fraser's C&J PR 3h after; s4.7).
5) Optional nightly inspiratory muscle training.
CONFLICTS: seiler (80/20 volume vs interval-led, low volume), bare (higher run/Zone 2 volume), first (3 quality runs vs 2 plus easy).

SEILER EVO 5 (running intensity distribution):
1) Count by SESSION, across the whole week (profile §4.1-2: stress is the session/day). Cap hard sessions at 2-3/wk TOTAL, metcons included [INFERENCE on metcons, §8]. 3-4 hard/wk for weeks risks overreaching (§4.5).
2) Runs 4/wk (Seiler gives no run count; recreational athletes are described as 4-5 sessions/wk, §8). Galloway/FIRST 3/wk is not supported by his work. FIRST's 3 runs are mostly hard, which is the opposite of 80/20.
- Sat: long Z1, 60 -> 90 min.
- 2 easy Z1 runs, 25-35 min, on lift days.
- 1 quality run, alternating weekly:
  (a) 4x8 min, 2 min rest, at maximal sustainable even effort (~90% HRmax). First-rep pace is held for all four. Start pace = 10k pace + 10-15 s/mi [INFERENCE], with 10k pace = T10k/6.214. Basis: Seiler 2013, §5.
  (b) Pyramidal/threshold: 3x10 min, 2 min rest, at ~85-90% HRmax. Start pace = 10k pace + 20-30 s/mi [INFERENCE]. The 2025 IPD meta-analysis Seiler co-authored favors pyramidal for recreational athletes (Evidence section).
3) Z1 = conversational, below ~75% HRmax, or RPE <=3/10 (§5). Gate it by HR/RPE, not pace. Easy days must stay easy: this is the 'black hole' rule (§4.7).
4) Hard days need >=1 easy or strength day between them [INFERENCE]. Never put a 4x8 and a long metcon on the same day.
5) Progress by adding Z1 duration and frequency, not intensity (§6).
EXPECTED CONFLICTS:
- glassman: metcon frequency and intensity counted as hard days.
- FIRST: 3 quality runs/wk vs 80/20.
- nick-bare / wendler: stacking quality runs on squat/deadlift days.

PROFILE DONE: /Users/jason/Documents/golden-hour/profiles/first-running-frequency.md
EVIDENCE FIRST: 3 runs/wk is a well-supported MINIMUM effective dose, not a proven optimum. Pollock 1977 found fitness rose in direct proportion to frequency (1/3/5 d), with injury at 0/12/39% in untrained joggers. Wenger&Bell 1986 pooled optimum was 4x/wk, and fit people (VO2 >50) need at least 3. Hard sessions plateau at 2-3/wk (Yang 2025, Lenk 2025). Galloway's plateau claim is only secondhand and no cited study was found (Profile, Frequency evidence).
RECS (P10 = 10k time / 6.214, in s/mi):
- Tue SPEED: rotate 8-12x400 @P10-55..60, 6-8x800 @P10-45..50, 4-5x1200 @P10-40..45, 3-4x1600 @P10-35..40, with 400m jog between. Build to about 5 km of reps by week 5.
- Thu TEMPO: 3-4 mi @P10, or 5 mi @P10+15..20. Fits the 60-min cap.
- Sat LONG: @P10+60..75. Cap each long run at 110% of the longest run in the prior 30 days (Frandsen 2025). This replaces the old 10%/2wk rule.
- 2x HARD cross-training, about 40 min (assault bike or rower at the rec center), on non-run days. FIRST says easy cross-training wastes the session.
- Optional 4th run from week 5, only if there are no niggles: 25-30 min easy. This departs from FIRST's 'no more than 3', justified by the newer evidence above.
- Never double up on missed runs. Keep a non-running day before each key run (Galloway 48h).
CONFLICTS:
1. seiler: FIRST's 3 runs are all moderate or hard, not 80/20.
2. wendler: no squat/DL before Tue/Thu/Sat runs. Key runs need fresh legs.
3. glassman: do metcons count as my 'hard cross-training', and does that leave enough recovery?

(b) Paces come straight from a 10k result (s5).

Open: hinshaw's speed-gear formulas, if they differ from the FIRST table.
